A clue on the leaf

Little draws the head before a vein fork, then after it on the same leaf vein. The two marks are evidence — clues that can support an idea.

5

Hold, then reach

The prolegs anchor the rear: they hold it in place. The front stretches ahead as the body straightens.

4

The rear catches up

Front grips hold the leaf. The rear slides closer and the long middle lifts into a tall loop.

3

The arch begins

Little spots a green arch on the leaf. “A tiny bridge!” The arch flattens, and a small head reaches past a vein. Big watches from the path.

2

A pretend leaf route

“Does every loop go one inch?” Little asks. The name sounds like a ruler, but real steps vary.

6

A later shape

Little imagines later chapters. The caterpillar becomes a pupa, then a moth. That change of body form is metamorphosis, and it takes time.

7

Make a little book

  1. 1Fold it into 8 boxes. Open it flat.

  2. 2Fold short end to short end. Cut the thick line. Open it.

  3. 3Fold the long way, pictures out. Push the ends in.

  4. 4Fold into a book. Page 1 goes on the front!

8

Wonder Daily

A loop goes somewhere.
